- Row 8, the result grounds of imports: [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope), where a question owned by another member is decided from those members at their current digests or returns `out_of_frame`; [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#5-bounded-context-semantic-resolution), which refines the import rule between bounded contexts, and the [PRODUCT_DEFINITION family table](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#foundation-to-law-binding-a-project-to-the-method), whose sixth row applies the rule to an activation that reports a missing binding before relying on the concept.
- Row 9, the three inputs, gaps, survival and predicates travel: [ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability), where a required result that is absent, stale or bound to another subject cannot satisfy a dependent conjunction and a `satisfied` for the declared disjunction counts toward no other predicate, and [§3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition); [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), Protocol, where a result bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment, and [§4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results), which keeps findings apart from undecided predicates and uncovered coverage; [ASSURANCE §7 The set](ASSURANCE.md#the-set), [§10](ASSURANCE.md#10-testing-evidence-composition), where a missing result stays visible under aggregate green status, and [§13 Claim boundaries](ASSURANCE.md#claim-boundaries), where an unselected claim is uncovered coverage; [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4 AC-007](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal), where a refusal keeps its predicate and `refusal(basis)` is a closed result, not a gap; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE Drift locks](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#drift-locks), coverage-and-return lock, and [§11 Refinement and conjunction](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#refinement-and-conjunction), where a seam without a result is a gap; [REFERENCE_FRAME §5 Method functions](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#5-method-functions), where gaps are no outcome of `conjoin` and are recorded beside the reported value, [§6 Result conjunction](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#result-conjunction) and [§8 Coverage ledger](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#coverage-ledger), where an uncovered row is uncovered coverage, never a `falsified` component; [TICKETS §7 Condition-based closure and reuse](TICKETS.md#condition-based-closure-and-reuse), where the closing condition is the conjunction with the declared obligations as required coverage; [ODD §11.5D](ODD.md#115d-constructive-evaluation-and-yield-loop) and [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE Closed constraint, judgment, residual and stop kinds](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md#closed-constraint-judgment-residual-and-stop-kinds), where no value counts toward another predicate and a `partial_effect` residual survives every join; [UX §15](UX.md#15-results-of-this-profile) and [WORLD_MODEL §14](WORLD_MODEL.md#14-results-of-this-profile), with the [WORLD_MODEL family table](WORLD_MODEL.md#foundation-to-law), whose row for the Markov-object construct lets a failed run falsify that run's predicate only; [CONFORMANCE §5](CONFORMANCE.md#5-discriminator-coverage), discriminators 23 and 24, and [§2](CONFORMANCE.md#2-construction-trials), trial T-04.
- Row 10, stale results: [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE Drift locks](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#drift-locks), where a stale held result before disposition is a gap, never relabelled `invalid_basis`, and [§11 Refinement and conjunction](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#refinement-and-conjunction); [ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability), for a required result bound to another basis; [REFERENCE_FRAME §8 Coverage ledger](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#coverage-ledger), where a stale coverage tuple returns `invalid_basis` for the audit's own predicate; [EVALUATION §7 Method self-qualification](EVALUATION.md#method-self-qualification), the `conjoin` row of its population table; [CONFORMANCE §5](CONFORMANCE.md#5-discriminator-coverage), discriminator 24.

- Row 18, the formal fragment: [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §1](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#1-position), for category-theoretic status, and [§5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds), where a model claiming functor laws carries the demonstration; [EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations), Equivalence ladder, where a categorical equivalence claim meets each applicable item; [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding), rule 4, where a claim that a binding preserves categorical structure meets it; [CONFORMANCE §5](CONFORMANCE.md#5-discriminator-coverage), discriminator 51.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

### Conjunction of results

Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
what it requires.

A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):

- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
  composite basis, and which do not.

A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.

Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

Predicates travel. Each component keeps its predicate and domain outcome
through every join, so an uncertain effect stays distinct from a failure
and from an undecided claim, and a `satisfied` for one predicate never
counts toward another: a step's `satisfied` for "a candidate is available"
never counts toward the candidate's fitness or acceptance.

Reported value. The conjunction is `satisfied` only when every mandatory
result is `satisfied` with valid applicable evidence, the declared basis
relations agree, and the second and third inputs are empty. A composite
with a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint or an uncovered
required obligation cannot project success. Where a mandatory result is
not `satisfied`, the conjunction
reports a non-satisfied value chosen by its declared rule from those
returned; no universal order among the non-satisfied values exists, and
the member or profile that applies the conjunction declares its own in
its declared rule. Where every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`
and the declared basis relations disagree, the conjunction reports
`invalid_basis`, because no coherent composite basis supports the
composite predicate (§2, Basis); any gaps stay recorded by kind. Where
every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`, the declared basis
relations agree and a gap remains, the conjunction reports
`indeterminate`, because the results it holds cannot decide the composite
predicate; that value is the conjunction's own, and the gaps stay
recorded by kind. A `falsified` result that is not mandatory stays in the
conjunction's record with its predicate and is never discarded. Where
every mandatory result is `satisfied`, the declared basis relations agree
and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint
falsifies the conjunction whichever contributor found it, and without one
the conjunction's value is the one its declared rule gives over the
mandatory results.

The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

### Assurance relations

For a deciding rule, use [Preservation through construction](#preservation-through-construction),
[Assertions and observation](#assertions-and-observation),
[Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance),
[Quantified assurance](#quantified-assurance), or
[Change impact and evidence reuse](#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse).
The family table below explains those owners and adds no separate decision.

The relations below connect construction to the assertions, observations
and evidence that support claims about it. They are the shared owner for
the preservation, assertion, provenance, quantified-assurance, reuse and
formal-representation obligations in this corpus; ACTIVATION §1, §4, §5 and §7, EVALUATION §1 and §3,
ASSURANCE §3, §10, §11 and §14, RELEASE §8 and §9, SPEC_METHOD §4 and
any a_c interpretation apply them and state no second relation (P6).
A tenant chooses its representation and execution within these obligations. The notation
states proof obligations; writing an implication does not discharge it.

Foundation to law. This family, assurance relations, covers the six
subsections that follow. Its instance premises are: (a) a construction
with the governing basis bound at intake under ACTIVATION §1 and the
material assumptions, together written Γ here; (b) a declared domain Ω of cases, each with the inputs,
behaviour and environment material to an obligation; (c) a checker with
declared observations and an admitted evaluation relation. They are
conditions of the situations the family governs, not commitments.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing this section does not
(P2, P6).

### Preservation through construction

A construction binds its starting state A and required outcome Z under
[ACTIVATION §1 Construction relation](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation);
the governing basis bound at its intake and the material assumptions are
together written Γ here. The
predicate for Z includes required effects and trace properties where
these matter.

For a sequence of transformations, let `X_i` be the state or trace domain
at boundary i, `F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1)` the declared transition relation, and
`P_i` the property to retain or establish there. A claimed preservation
step has the form:

```text
For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').
```

The relation accounts for the outcomes, effects and assumptions material
to the claim. A relation covering successful completion alone supplies no
claim about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects; those
cases follow Results above and the result, authority and recovery
contracts of ACTIVATION §3 and §5. The real execution's conformance to
the relation is a separate obligation (P4a, P1, P6).

An end-to-end argument establishes the initial condition, each step's
applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the
connection from the final property to Z. The preceding postcondition
must establish the next precondition, or the missing condition must be
acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects
require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not
establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition
compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination
and the availability of a suitable next step (P4a, P2, P6).

Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate
transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound
for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or
to remain unchanged. [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement),
Exact and approximate steps, owns the per-step law and applies this
obligation to refinement steps. A
change to the governing outcome or meaning follows its owner and the
successor rules of SPEC_METHOD §4 and RELEASE §9 (P1, P6).

The algorithmic account states the required operation, the informational
account the meaning and distinctions retained, and the computational
binding how work and observations are realised
([§2 Accounts of a construction](#accounts-of-a-construction)). A claim
across these accounts identifies its maps and preservation obligations;
execution by a person, a machine or a mixed arrangement does not
discharge them by itself. A commuting diagram, functor or equivalence
claim requires the categorical demonstration above (P1, P6).

### Assertions and observation

For a selected source obligation r, let `Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω)` be its
required predicate over the declared domain Ω of cases. The interpretation
retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted
alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected
text; it does not prove the interpretation faithful (P1, P3).

An assertion targets a predicate `q_t` and states whether that predicate
is the full obligation or a narrower claim. The directions differ:

```text
Q_r implies q_t                   : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.
q_t implies Q_r                   : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.
```

These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a
necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction
requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of
passing tests does not supply it by its count (P1, P6, P5).

Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and
`T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R is the core result
algebra of Results above. A deterministic checker is a functional special
case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on
the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted
conclusions, not a favourable selected run. `indeterminate` is the core
judgment whose admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate (Results).
It is distinct from an evaluation that was not performed, and from work
or coverage that remains unresolved, which is a state of the work
([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),
[§5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) and not a judgment value.
Writing `sat` and `fal` for the satisfied and falsified judgments about
`q_t`, not new execution states:

```text
For every s in Ω:
  (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).
  (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).
```

The candidate identifies what supports each claimed direction and where
it is unresolved. A relation admitting both a sound satisfied judgment
and an indeterminate judgment need not always decide the case. A
restricted deterministic model retains its scope, and an actual checker
requires its own conformance account. An observed test pass remains an
observation while the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not
become established satisfaction of the source obligation, and a reported
failure is treated the same way. The observation binding itself needs
support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or
execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim
uses its declared distribution over outcomes under Quantified assurance
below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities (P6, P5, P1).

Observation sufficiency. A checker that always decides `q_t` correctly
from π alone requires:

```text
For all s, s' in Ω:
  π(s) = π(s')  implies  q_t(s) = q_t(s').
```

If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth
values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between
them; further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate
judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a
predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision
procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations
retain their distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was
not performed (Results) (P3, P1, P5, P6).

Where a representation is claimed sufficient for subsequent decisions,
identify the consumer-required observations and readouts and material
applicability conditions, directly or by reference to the consuming contract.
Identify input and policy scope and horizon where the claim depends on them.
Retain the standing, obligations, currentness and invalidation, causal
producer and authority distinctions those consumers require. Two cases with
the same representation but incompatible required decisions under those
fixed conditions falsify the sufficiency claim. This requires no anticipation
of all future uses (P1, P2, P6).

When a chosen functional account claims decision preservation, define its
functions and domain: s is a state, u a permitted input under the fixed
conditions Γ, alpha maps states to representations, delta(s,u) is the
consumer's decision, and delta_hat is that decision on representations.
Demonstrate `delta(s,u) = delta_hat(alpha(s),u)` on the declared domain
(equivalently factor delta through alpha with u held fixed). When it
claims transition preservation, also demonstrate
`alpha(T(s,u)) ≈ T_hat(alpha(s),u)`, where T and T_hat are the state and
representation transitions and ≈ is the declared adequacy relation, and
demonstrate the declared readout preservation on
that domain and horizon. Other frames preserve their consumer-required
relational distinctions under the owning contracts; these equations impose
no universal functional model or executable decision procedure. Mandatory
authority and hold distinctions remain exact where their contracts require
exactness. Approximation needs explicit latitude and a justified horizon
bound; a one-step bound alone supplies no multi-step guarantee (P1, P4a, P6).

The [one-assessment example](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#continuation-sensitive-sufficiency)
separates an unperformed assessment from a closed indeterminate assessment.
Its four-state representation retains every modeled state distinction under
fixed conditions Γ. It is a sufficiency witness with no state aggregation,
not a proof of compression, minimal context or general task selection. A
smallest or cheapest sufficient-material claim needs its own objective,
scope and evidence; representation size and total operating cost are
different quantities (P2, P6).

### Parallel derivation and mutual assurance

Construction and assurance can follow different paths from a common
obligation. For `requirement → refinement → realisation`, assertions
derived from the requirement check its applicable conditions in the
realisation; assertions derived from the refinement check its more
detailed obligations there. Acceptance tests and build-level tests can
instantiate these paths
([ASSURANCE §14](ASSURANCE.md#14-design-to-module-evidence-route)); the
roles identify the selected sources and subject in this example and
prescribe no stage names or test classes (P1, P6).

An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the
owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared
dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).

An implementation-derived test can be useful for regression or a stated
local property. Repeating the implementation's decision supplies no
independent justification of its fidelity to an upstream obligation. A
shorter assertion path can be easier to inspect and execute than
construction; that is a supported design claim for the selected path, not
a guarantee of correctness, coverage or independence. Valid distinct
implementations can produce different outputs within the same acceptable
relation; equality of outputs is not always the oracle (P1, P6).

Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or
assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both
being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis
([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation))
and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Assurance accounts for
shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,
copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors,
model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence.
Porting retains authorship and common dependencies
([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)). Repeating
evidence does not create a new independent observation. Agreement with
an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired
real-world outcome; validation of the governing expectations uses its
declared purpose and external observations through their owners, and
proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow the applicable
change authority ([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#4-change-management))
(P4a, P6, P1).

These relationships are recoverable from the existing sources, bindings
and evidence carriers. Shared derivations can be recorded once and applied
to a declared family. No new per-test document, parallel ledger, fixed
number of reviewers or prescribed provenance format is required (P6).

### Quantified assurance

Risk model. The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required
assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That
selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and
uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional
evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and
dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks
substitutes for that account (P6, P5).

Where quantified assurance is claimed, its model states the population or
uncertainty being modelled, prior information, likelihoods, shared causes
and calibration limits. For a specified violation event V and evidence
event E:

```text
P(V | E, Γ) =
  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)
  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].
```

The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other
observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions
matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior, and a
numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and evidence.

Let `M_i` mean that check i misses V under the specified evaluation
conditions. The joint miss probability factors exactly by conditional
probabilities:

```text
P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ)
  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).
```

Conditional terms require defined conditioning events; zero-probability
prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing
those terms with `P(M_i | V, Γ)` requires conditional independence under
the declared model. One minus the joint miss probability is the chance of
at least one detection under those same conditions; it is not the
probability that the whole product is correct. Agreement does not
necessarily increase confidence when shared causes or new information
change the model (P6, P1).

Calibration from sampled cases or injected defects supports only its
justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numeric
confidence remains unresolved; qualitative evidence and stated limits
remain usable within the governing policy. No universal probability
threshold is imposed and no probability estimate is required for every
test. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be
waived by a cheaper assurance plan (P5, P6).

### Change impact and evidence reuse

Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct
dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an
obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,
conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,
instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A
requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model (P3, P6).

Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly
discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed
facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover
the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use
of evidence. A candidate selection is:

```text
S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.
```

The representation of these dependencies is the tenant's choice; no
exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires
supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change
cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not
evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves
the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create
assessment work even when no existing check covers them. A mandatory
gate, an assessment that the governing policy requires irrespective of
selection ([RELEASE §8](RELEASE.md#8-acceptance)), remains applicable
(P5, P6).

For a new subject and basis, let `E_old` be the existing evidence records,
`E_reassessed` the evidence newly produced by reassessment, and `E_new`
the resulting account. Reassessment includes the checks selected in
`S_Δ`, the assessment of new obligations and the applicable mandatory
gates. Selection alone produces no execution evidence; failed and
indeterminate results retain their standing:

```text
E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.
```

Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new
subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and
observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are
unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The
original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability
relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither
invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run is not an unchanged independent
test of the correction: the corrected subject carries its own evidence.
Known failures, unresolved coverage and their
citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an
authorised change of obligation disposes of them (P3, P4b, P6).

If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need
authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a
refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the
requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation
reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the
still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,
not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and
invalidates affected claims; it need not erase valid work or rerun every
check ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) (P3, P6).

The governing assurance can be established from applicable retained
evidence together with new evidence; the completeness of that account is
distinct from the freshness of every execution. Selection considers
impact-analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs together,
with anticipated costs distinguished from measurements
([ACTIVATION §6](ACTIVATION.md#6-cost-and-proportionality)). The
required assurance, risk policy and mandatory gates constrain that
optimisation; a cheap selection that leaves a required obligation
uncovered is insufficient. Broad or
uncertain impact, a change to the selection model, an applicable release
rule or evidence that selection missed a dependency can justify wider
testing; full-suite execution remains available and may itself have
coverage gaps. No universal full-suite cadence follows, and no
optimisation removes a separately required gate. Failures enter diagnosis
and an authorised response
([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation));
the next selected action may acquire evidence before any repair is
justified. [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse)
applies this relation to closed results and handoffs; its three
invalidators are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected when
its `D*(t)` meets `I(Δ)` (P5, P6).

### Formal representation

An a_c interpretation of these assurance relations represents their
material obligations and dependency relationships. Its fidelity and the
acquired views that project it follow
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §6](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#6-interpretation-and-models)
and [Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).
It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a
stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked
structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.
An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to
establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.
No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is
selected (P1, P6).

Assessment of these assurance relations demonstrates the applicable
positive, negative and unresolved cases in [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md),
including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection
that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence.
Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and
observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove
the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain
unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their
governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).

Assessment of these owners and their consumers follows
[EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations) and
[§7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method).
Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate
evidence within the applicable conformance and qualification criteria;
these obligations do not make each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).

Purpose and material relation of the assurance relations: they connect
construction results to the obligations they support, expose shared
errors, and direct reassessment to affected claims while retaining
evidence whose applicability is established (P6, P2).

## 5. Hypotheses

Not law; carried for falsification: categorical equivalence of 𝒜 and ℐ under
some reformulation; universal algorithmic capture of meaning; the statistical
Markov boundary (candidate status under
[WORLD_MODEL §4](WORLD_MODEL.md#epistemic-status));
traversal composition laws of any runtime.

# Source-first expectation report: STDO 3.1.0-rc.2 W35 successor-conservation repair

## 0. Standing of this report

- **What this is:** expectations written before seeing any candidate. It contains no verdict on any candidate, no repair proposal and no publication authority.
- **What I read:** only the supplied packet. I compared the supplied texts by reading them. The only hash comparisons I rely on are the ones the operator computed.
- **Tool use:** none. I made no tool calls, including the advisor tool, because the instruction said not to use tools. I read no files and ran no commands.
- **Host context:** the host injected an account-identity reminder and environment metadata. I did not use either. All other hidden host or system context is unmeasured.
- **Who I am:** a Claude-family actor. I authored neither the candidate nor any governing source. Native CLI metadata, not this text, is authoritative for my session identity.
- **Main limit:** I could not see W35's rule text, the index, the query or fact schema, or the meaning of the boundary values. Every expectation below that depends on them is conditional, and §5 lists them as gaps.

## 1. Expected behaviour by boundary

A "fact" here is a value the query declares, such as which boundary is being decided or whether the subject is a successor.

| Query case | What W35 should do | Depends on | Must not be transferred in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Product acceptance of a successor subject** | W35 is present, with its full meaning (§2). RC1 shows the defect as absent; RC2 must show it present. | Acceptance relies on qualified claims: an unresolved disposition blocks qualification "and so cannot be accepted" (EVALUATION §5 ¶2). Any rule W35 declares as a dependency (for example evidence reuse or result conjunction) must also be selected. | Release-only conditions: atomic 25-ref push, per-ref leases, remote-absence checks, selector advancement, cohort suffix equality, GitHub release, public readback. Also, RELEASE §8's acceptance criteria for an immutable cut must not be presented as the generic Product acceptance law. Acceptance authority stays with the decision owner. |
| **B. Product acceptance, subject not a successor** | The "where the subject is a successor" condition (EVALUATION §5) stays visible. No disposition record is demanded as if the condition held. | The successor trigger itself. | An unconditional "acceptance requires a disposition record" for a subject with no predecessor. |
| **C. Product acceptance, successor status unknown, null or ill-typed** | The condition stays open. If selection is gated on a fact, the result is incomplete or a material gap, never coverage (PC-R03, PC-S05). | — | Treating unknown as "not a successor". |
| **D. Qualification** | W35 present before and after; no regression. RELEASE §3 binds "the complete successor relation"; §9 says an unresolved disposition blocks qualification of the affected claim. | Exact-cut binding. | The human acceptance criterion and any claim of acceptance authority. |
| **E. Release** | W35 present before and after. RELEASE §8 requires the "successor relation stable" and the mandatory gates. | Qualification (D) and the §8 gates. | — (release conditions belong here) |
| **F. Ordinary work, incremental QA, landing, no boundary** | W35 not selected. No acceptance gate is implied. | EVALUATION §5 "Landing, closure and release"; PC-S02 (incremental QA cannot imply acceptance). | The acceptance-blocking predicate. Recording dispositions during construction or integration (RELEASE row 11 and the support-line paragraph) is a separate obligation, unchanged by this repair. |
| **G. Boundary fact unknown, null or ill-typed** | Incomplete, not covered. It must not default to ordinary work (which would drop W35) or to acceptance (which would assert false applicability). | PC-R03, PC-S05. | — |

**Constraint on how the repair is realised.** Two forms are admissible:
- W35 is selected at product acceptance and carries its source-owned successor condition inside the rule; or
- selection is gated on an existing declared fact, with unknown handled as in row C.

If the repair introduces a new purpose fact or changes what an existing fact means, that is a semantic change to the purpose (PC-S06, SDLC-WORKFLOW "existing purpose and fact meanings are preserved"). It would go beyond the activation's description of "a bounded realization/selection repair, not a change to the governing obligation", and it must be declared explicitly. Extra boolean facts must not make the obligation optional.

## 2. Obligations W35 must carry at successor acceptance

| # | Obligation | Source |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Acceptance evidence for a successor includes the successor disposition record. | EVALUATION §5 ¶2 |
| O2 | The record names the exact predecessor immutable cut, and that origin stays immutable for the candidate. | RELEASE §9 ¶1 |
| O3 | Every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor receives exactly one disposition: conserved, superseded (an accepted successor relation replaces it), intentionally removed (current Product authority removes it) or not applicable (with a bounded reason). | RELEASE §9 ¶1 |
| O4 | A claim with an unresolved disposition cannot be qualified, and so cannot be accepted. In conjunction it is a gap, a planned assessment without a closed result. It is not a falsified result. | EVALUATION §5; RELEASE §9; FOUNDATIONS Conjunction "Gaps" |
| O5 | "Conserved" is a semantic test made on the same material case, scope and authority. It covers what must happen, what may happen, what is prohibited, and what follows when a trigger, exception or premise is absent. It applies in the owning text and in the consumer bindings, with counterexamples. Obligation strength, preferences, exceptions and scope conditions must all survive. Naming, code similarity, patch absence or a whole-package equivalence statement prove nothing. | RELEASE §9 ¶3 |
| O6 | A "conserved" disposition recorded before this test applied is unresolved until re-evaluated. | RELEASE §9 ¶3 |
| O7 | A conserved reading made on an earlier successor text carries over only if the owning text and consumer bindings are unchanged, or the change is shown not to affect the claim (`retain_applicable`). | RELEASE §9 ¶2; FOUNDATIONS Change impact and evidence reuse |
| O8 | A disposition is a claim, not a result. Qualification records a core result for it. It is distinct from the decision owner's disposition of an assessed candidate (ACTIVATION §3). | RELEASE §9 ¶4 |
| O9 | "Intentionally removed" is a decision of the current Product authority, and the record is that decision. | EVALUATION §5 |
| O10 | Acceptance is the decision owner's act over an unchanged subject. A reviewer result is input, never closure. Green labels and counts are not acceptance. Index coverage grants no acceptance. | EVALUATION §5 ¶1; Purpose Context PRODUCT "makes no release decision" |

**Behaviour when a trigger, exception or premise is missing:**

| Situation | Expected outcome |
|---|---|
| Successor trigger absent | O1–O9 are not asserted. The general acceptance law still applies. |
| Trigger present, predecessor not named | O2 is unmet, so the claim cannot be qualified or accepted. |
| "Not applicable" without a bounded reason | Unresolved. |
| "Removed" without an authority decision | Unresolved. |
| Evidence binds an earlier text and no applicability is shown | Excluded by basis (EVALUATION §2). |

Deterministic-kind migration applies only if a successor adopts the total deterministic kind. I do not expect it at this boundary unless W35's source closure already includes it.

**Finite counterexamples W35 must expose.** Each is a falsifier for the RC2 product-acceptance context:

| ID | Scenario | Expected handling |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | Successor acceptance with no disposition record | W35 shows the block |
| K2 | Record says "conserved" on the strength of whole-package wording equivalence | Unresolved |
| K3 | Pre-test "conserved" disposition | Unresolved |
| K4 | "Removed" without a Product-authority decision | Unresolved |
| K5 | All dispositions resolved | Rendering must not imply acceptance follows |
| K6 | Rendering conflates disposition (claim) with acceptance disposition (result) | Conflation is a falsifier |
| K7 | RC1 conserved evidence reused after the bindings changed | Not retained without applicability |

## 3. Verification matrix (proportionate)

| Dimension | Kind of claim | Expected evidence | Not established by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Before/after** | Behaviour | Before the repair: on RC1's exact published package (index ID, manifest `ddbd…7faa`, query bytes, output), rows A, D and E reproduce "absent / present / present", and that failed expectation is retained. After: RC2 on rows A–G as in §1, with the before and after outputs kept as distinct subjects. | A label change, or a digest update alone (PC-S06) |
| **Structural content** | Structure | The RC2 indexes bind the actual RC2 native cut A, its tag object and the manager-produced manifest, not 3.0.4 or a predicted value. Source membership, order and bytes are bound. RC1, 3.0.4, 3.0.5 and development entries are byte-identical. The 39 unaffected rules are text-stable. Catalog, public-manifest and Skills pins are reconciled. No manifest contains its own hash. Six-Product version suffixes equal `3.1.0-rc.2`. | Semantic adequacy |
| **Semantic coverage** | Independent judgment | A new assessment of the RC2 index, corpus and query for the repaired acceptance context, including rows B–G, qualification, release and dependency guards. Codex authored the candidate and a Claude-family assessor is declared, so this is cross-family; same-family Codex checks count as mechanical only. Contexts never assessed stay `covered: false` or unknown. | Tests, checksums, author self-review, RC1 verdicts |
| **Actor and host behaviour** | Operational | Both installed host adapters resolve the same checked runtime (PC-R09). Explicit invocation, installed-layout behaviour and automatic discovery are reported as separate claims, and only observed modes are qualified. | Source success standing in for installed behaviour (RELEASE §3) |
| **Predecessor conservation** | Claim-level | RC1 → RC2 dispositions per affected Product claim. W35 gets an explicit entry (changed selection, unchanged obligation). Native selected owners are compared RC1 vs RC2 byte by byte; any changed owner (for example release-facing metadata) gets a claim-level reading. The earlier repairs (two stale-guide findings, missing-helper frame failure) are re-verified, including all 52 frame tests. Visual rebinding carries the predecessor/current identity and the source delta of its selected members. | A version-string change alone (PC-R16) |
| **Release identity** | Exact cut | Commit A, its local annotated tag and a private verified install; commit B; Product subtree roots and trees; member inventories. Remote absence of every RC2 immutable ref and no higher ordinal. Exact expected object IDs for mutable refs. One atomic transaction for 25 refs with no fallback. RC1 refs unmoved. A normal GitHub release. Downloaded assets match advertised and expected hashes. A fresh isolated-store install of the manager and native cut, with membership and context results verified. | Publication standing in for acceptance |
| **Exact-cut acceptance** | Human decision | Outside the publication evidence. Recorded as open until the human authority accepts the exact cut identity. | Publication, qualification, review results |

My own consistency arithmetic gives 25 refs as 6 Products × 4 (RC tag, selector, RC branch, release branch) + 1 carrier. That is my inference only; no source supplied says so.

## 4. Evidence reuse rules and what I will need later

**Reuse rules:**
- RC1 evidence keeps its original subject. It can be used for RC2 only under `retain_applicable`: the claim and scope still apply, the assertion and observation basis is still justified, and the dependencies are unchanged or covered by a preservation relation.
- RC1 exact-query assessments are never relabelled as RC2 results (PC-S09, PC-R16). They may be cited as prior evidence.
- Mechanical evidence may be shared; judgments may not (EVALUATION §3).
- The W35 counterexample is later counterevidence. Any RC1 verdict that depended on acceptance coverage for the affected query is invalidated for that claim, and the record must say so rather than delete it (EVALUATION §1).
- Mandatory gates (RELEASE §8) stay in force even where evidence is reused.

**Bytes, queries and evidence I will need:**
1. The RC1 and RC2 W35 rule objects: text, conditions, exceptions, dependencies and grounds.
2. The full rule-set diff, which should show only the W35 selection change.
3. The SDLC purpose definition and its fact schema, including the boundary values and their meanings.
4. The exact queries for rows A–G, with outputs from RC1 and RC2.
5. RC2 native A: commit, tag object and manifest. The selected-owner byte comparison RC1 vs RC2.
6. The catalog, public manifest, coverage-standing records and Skills dependency pins.
7. The disposition and impact record.
8. Outputs of the 52 frame tests and the current-state checks.
9. Both host-adapter observations.
10. Commit B, the cohort record, the ref graph with remote expected and absent states, the GitHub asset hashes and the fresh-install readback.
11. The Python RC2 entry's binding and its coverage-standing record.

## 5. Gaps, ambiguities and limits

**Missing sources and the predicates they leave unresolved:**
- **What "product_acceptance" means:** this is owned by the Purpose Context SDLC purpose (`skills/stdo-context/references/sdlc-workflow.md` and the authoring inputs for the RC1 SDLC entry). Without it, I cannot decide whether this boundary includes acceptance of an immutable release cut, which would bring in RELEASE §8. Rows A, B and C stay conditional.
- **Parts of the method not supplied:** TICKETS, SPEC_METHOD, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, ACTIVATION §1–§5, `method-targets.md`, the Skills and visual Product documents, the RC1 cohort record and the RC2 root RELEASE record. These own boundary policy, the independence boundaries (UP-007) and the visual and Skills claims. I made no expectations that depend on them.

**Reading observations (by eye, not by byte diff):**
- Native RC1 RELEASE and installed 3.0.4 RELEASE differ in §7: RC1 adds "Source freeze and stable cohort construction" and rewrites the lead-in to the two-commit paragraph. The texts of §3, §8 and §9 look identical.
- EVALUATION is byte-equal between the two, per the operator's hash.
- This supports "native law is already correct" for W35's owning sections, but only as a reading.

**Adjacent observation, not part of this repair:** if the preserved development SDLC entry shares W35's selection, it carries the same historical defect. It stays immutable and goes back to its owner with no repair here.

**Not done:** I examined no candidate, executed nothing, verified no hashes, and claim no whole-method or universal context-fit result. I use no numeric severity scale; materiality is stated as the affected predicate (product-acceptance coverage, qualification and release regression, false applicability, unknown handling).

# Source-only addendum: what `product_acceptance` means, the successor condition, dependency guards, and corrections (STDO 3.1.0-rc.2, acceptance selector)

## 0. Standing

- **What this is:** expectations written from the supplied sources only, before seeing any candidate. It contains no candidate verdict, no patch and no publication authority.
- **Tools:** I made no tool calls, including the advisor tool, because the instruction said not to use tools. The host account reminder and environment metadata were not used. Any other hidden host context is unmeasured.
- **What I did not see:** the W35 rule object, the rule index, the query, RC2 bytes, test output and any verdict. `context_core.py` (the rendering and guard logic) was not supplied either, so anything below about rendering is a requirement drawn from the authoring contract. It is not a description of how the engine actually behaves.
- **Citation key:**
  - **P** = PURPOSE.json
  - **U** = references/sdlc-workflow.md
  - **M** = references/method-targets.md
  - **D** = design/DESIGN.md
  - **S** = requirements/SDLC-WORKFLOW.md
  - **R** = requirements/README.md
  - **A** = references/authoring.md
  - **E5** = installed EVALUATION §5
  - **R9** = installed RELEASE §9
  - **PA** = the prior source-only Claude report

## 1. What `product_acceptance` denotes, and what its name does not establish

**Declared meaning.** `boundary_kind` is "The actual decision boundary: none, landing, work_closure, product_acceptance, qualification, or release. A name does not establish its conditions or authority." (P). U adds: "the selected boundary's actual conditions remain to be established", and "Named landing, closure, acceptance, qualification and release decisions retain their own conditions … they create no extra lifecycle or universal review gate."

**My reading.** The value records an observation by the caller: the actual decision in this request is an acceptance decision. This is the decision E5 separates from the others: "Record these as separate decisions" (landing, work closure, release). It means acceptance as E5 ¶1 describes it: "the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject". That law is general. It is not limited to one named boundary, and its successor clause ("Where the subject is a successor…", E5 ¶2) is a condition on the subject, not on the label.

**What the label does not establish:**

| # | Not inferable from `boundary_kind = product_acceptance` | Source |
|---|---|---|
| N1 | That acceptance occurred, is authorized, or that any condition is met | P "A name does not establish its conditions or authority"; S coverage predicate; U "Neither … authorizes a boundary" |
| N2 | Who the decision owner is, or whether a bounded proxy was admitted | E5 ¶1 |
| N3 | That a declared cross-Product acceptance gate exists. That kind of gate requires an explicit declaration naming both Products, the relation, the candidate, review, conditions and owner. | E5 "Declared Product acceptance gates": "co-location, a dependency or this available mechanism creates none" |
| N4 | That the subject is a successor. No declared fact carries successor status (see §2). | P fact list |
| N5 | That this is acceptance of an immutable release cut. `release` is a separate value, and E5 says "release applies the separately selected publication and acceptance conditions of RELEASE". If a request accepts an exact cut, whether the caller labels it `product_acceptance` or `release` is the caller's observation. The supplied sources do not settle it. | P; E5 "Landing, closure and release" |
| N6 | Which review, independence or Product cutoff policy applies, or whether review is required | E5 "A required review holds…"; "The decision cutoff is the adopting Product's policy"; S PC-S04 |
| N7 | Any relation between `boundary_kind` and `action`. For example, nothing says whether `product_acceptance` is only meaningful when `action = boundary`. | No supplied source (gap G2) |

## 2. Can the existing successor condition stay in rule text without a new fact? Yes, lawfully, and this is my own reading.

- **No successor fact exists.** The 15 declared facts are listed in P. None of them means "the subject is a successor". `reuse_evidence` and `source_changed` mean other things, and reading them as a successor flag would change their declared meanings.
- **Keeping the condition as text is lawful, and is what the sources prescribe:**
  - A: "Use only declared purpose fact names and predicates justified by the source. Preserve richer conditions as text … rather than manufacturing facts"
  - A: "Do not … turn conditional rules into universal ones"
  - D: "Rich causal, permission, review and policy premises stay complete conditional obligations; query flags do not purport to prove future work"
  - S: "Complete conditional obligations name the evidence and owning Product inputs the consumer must obtain"
- **A new fact would be out of scope.** Adding a successor fact, or changing an existing fact's meaning, is a semantic purpose change: S "existing purpose and fact meanings are preserved unless an explicit semantic change establishes a new purpose boundary"; S PC-S06. That falls outside the admitted outcome ("purpose/fact meanings remain unchanged").
- **What may change.** D, "Latest method source rebinding", allows the purpose *description* to change to name the newly selected release while the purpose ID and fact meanings stay the same.
- **The text must keep four things, uninverted:**
  - the condition "where the subject is a successor" (E5 ¶2);
  - its population: "every predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor" (R9 ¶1);
  - the consumer's duty to establish successor status from task inputs;
  - when the condition is absent, the general acceptance law of E5 ¶1 still applies.
- **Open representational point (gap G3).** The sources do not decide whether the in-text successor condition must also appear as a material rule `unknown`, which would block a covered claim (A: "Rule `unknowns` are material when that rule is selected"). The rule is still selectable from `boundary_kind`, and the successor branch is a complete conditional instruction, so I count either representation as lawful. It becomes a falsifier only if the condition is dropped, made universal, or replaced by a manufactured fact.

## 3. Rendered dependency rules whose own guards are false or unknown

**Source law:**
- A: "Dependencies retain other local rules together; a false dependency remains visibly inapplicable."
- A: "A missing, null or incompatible fact yields unknown."
- A: "Unknown exception applicability prevents a covered claim."
- S: "Unknown facts deciding which constraints apply remain material gaps."
- A: "Similar labels do not establish either relation." Each dependency must be warranted by a source.

**Expectations for the later assessor:**

| # | Situation | Expected rendering and standing |
|---|---|---|
| X1 | Dependency guard false (e.g. `reuse_evidence = false`, `review_in_scope = false`, `profile_executive = false`) | The dependency is delivered with the dependent rule and is visibly inapplicable. It is not silently dropped and not shown as binding. |
| X2 | Dependency guard unknown | Retained and marked unknown, not false and not true. It is a material gap, and no covered claim follows. |
| X3 | A false or inapplicable dependency must not empty out the selected rule | If any of O1–O9 (PA §2) exists only inside a dependency whose guard is false at `product_acceptance`, the obligation is effectively absent. That is a falsifier. |
| X4 | A false fact must not hide a known applicability | P: `finding_present`, `reuse_evidence` and `source_changed` set false "must not conceal" known matters. `profile_executive` false "does not waive required assessment". A false `review_in_scope` does not waive a required review (S PC-S04; E5). |
| X5 | Selection is not truth | Rendering the dependency does not make its premise true. A passing `check` stays `covered: false` (U). |

## 4. Prior-actor expectations that need qualification or correction

The left column is what the prior report said. The right column is my correction.

| PA item | Correction or qualification |
|---|---|
| Row B and Row C (successor yes/no/unknown as query cases) | **Correct.** No successor fact exists, so these are not selector cases. Rows A, B and C get the same selection result. Row C's substance moves into the obligation the consumer applies: unestablished successor status must not be treated as "not a successor". |
| "Two admissible forms"; second: "selection gated on an existing declared fact" | **Qualify.** No existing declared fact denotes successor status. Selection can only turn on existing facts such as `boundary_kind` and `action`, with the successor condition kept in text (§2). A successor fact is outside the admitted outcome. |
| Row G "Boundary fact unknown → incomplete" | **Correct.** D says the family guard covers SDLC scope and adopted defaults. Named boundaries are rule conditions. An unknown `boundary_kind` therefore makes W35's own guard unknown (a material gap, not covered). It does not make the family selection "incomplete". Family-level incomplete applies only to family facts (U; R PC-R03). |
| Row G, implicit | **Add (gap G1).** An out-of-list string such as `"acceptance"` is type-compatible, so the scalar test `eq` gives false, not unknown (A). The supplied sources contain no value-list validation. A misspelled value could therefore quietly deselect W35. |

| Row D and Row E citations to RELEASE §3 and §8 | **Qualify.** They were not supplied in this packet. Only R9 ("blocks qualification") and E5 ("release applies … acceptance conditions of RELEASE") are re-grounded here. The regression expectation that W35 stays present at qualification and release is still source-supported. |

If the stated closing condition names acceptance or qualification, that relation comes from the task's condition, not from a selector fact. |

For RC1 → RC2, every rule other than W35 needs its meaning conserved, and each byte change (e.g. W01 release identity, the purpose description) needs an individual disposition (R9; S rebuild paragraph). Fact meanings must be semantically unchanged. |

## 5. Fixed falsifiers for the later candidate assessor

| ID | Falsifier |
|---|---|
| F1 | At `boundary_kind = product_acceptance`, W35's obligation (O1–O9) is not delivered, or reaches the reader only through a dependency that is false or inapplicable (X3). |
| F2 | The successor condition is removed, made universal, or turned into a manufactured fact, or the predecessor-claim population is narrowed. |
| F3 | A new purpose fact is added, or an existing fact's meaning changes (rather than just the release-naming description). |
| F4 | An unknown, null or ill-typed `boundary_kind` yields W35 as false or covered rather than unknown, or the family result is misreported. |
| F5 | W35 is no longer present at `qualification` or `release`, compared with the predecessor. |
| F6 | W35 is selected at `none`, `landing` or ordinary QA as if it were an acceptance gate (S PC-S02). |
| F7 | A dependency with a false guard is omitted or shown as binding, or one with an unknown guard is shown as resolved. |
| F8 | Any rendering, check or label implies that acceptance, qualification or coverage passed, or that a declared cross-Product gate exists (N1, N3). |
| F9 | Changes to rules other than W35, or to fact meanings, appear without individual dispositions. RC1 assessments are reused for RC2's index, corpus or query (M; R PC-R16; S PC-S09). |

# Independent assessment of the frozen STDO 3.1.0-rc.2 W35 repair subject

**Verdict.** The repair holds. W35 now applies at `product_acceptance` and is still selected at `qualification` and `release`. Its source-owned successor condition stays in the rule text, and no fact was added or redefined. Release-only duties are not imported at acceptance. All six constructed queries are **supported** for their exact subjects, with the residuals listed below. The three unknown-boundary queries are **refused correctly**. That is a fail-closed outcome, not semantic coverage. I found **no material counterexample** and no required owner re-entry for this bounded release.

## 0. Standing and limits

- **Identity.** I am a Claude-family actor; the environment reports `claude-opus-5-5`, and the CLI metadata is the authoritative identity. I authored no candidate. The Writers are Codex-family, so this judgment is cross-family. I am the same family as both source-first actors and the RC1 assessors, so confirmation bias is possible.
- **Tools.** I used none. An `advisor` tool was exposed in this session; I did not call it, because you prohibited tools. I recomputed no hashes. Every digest, byte equality and test result below is an operator or Writer observation.
- **Order of reading.** Sources and candidate arrived in one packet, so source-first order was not enforced in this session. Only the two fixed expectation reports predate exposure to the candidate.
- **What I read.** The full RC2 SDLC index and all six delivered bodies. Each deciding owner section: EVALUATION §5, RELEASE §8/§9, FOUNDATIONS Conjunction, ACTIVATION Applicability. The catalog and runtime code, and the native patch.
- **Python index.** For its 113 rules I relied on reported zero rule change and owner byte-equality, plus targeted re-reading. I did not re-derive every clause.
- **Hidden host context.** Not measured.

## 1. Conclusions by claim

### W35 repair (SDLC canonical index `39f2432c…`)

- **Scope of change (operator).** Only W35's `when` changed. Text, dependencies and source references are unchanged. The family guard and purpose facts are equal to RC1; only the purpose description changed.
- **Obligations carried at acceptance (my reading).** The rule carries, in substance, these obligations from my source-first report:
  - O1/O2: identify the exact immutable predecessor.
  - O3: four disposition values, including removal "by Product authority".
  - O4: an unresolved disposition "blocks … and has no performed result".
  - O5: comparing wording or digests alone is not conservation.
  - O7: reuse prior evidence without copying the old judgment.
- **Successor condition.** It stays textual ("For a successor qualification/acceptance claim"). It is not made universal and not turned into a fact.
- **Unestablished successor status.** It is withheld by W23 ("Unknown mandatory applicability … withholds the dependent claim"), not read as "not a successor".
- **Authority boundary.** The general acceptance and authority boundaries are carried by W02, W04, W06, W23 and W24. W25 states that a gate exists only by explicit declaration. The delivered body says "unassessed / experimental-candidate" and implies no acceptance.
- **Residuals.** These are compressions, not inversions (R1–R3 below):
  - the step from "blocks qualification" to "cannot be accepted" is left implicit;
  - the rule that a pre-test "conserved" disposition is unresolved is not stated;

### Unknown-boundary expectation revised

My addendum said an unknown `boundary_kind` should make W35's own guard unknown, not make the family incomplete. That was conditional on not seeing the catalog. The actual catalog `family_guard` (identical in RC1 and RC2) includes `any` over all six boundary values, so `boundary_kind` is a family fact. PC-R03 therefore requires family `incomplete`. The three actual refusals match this exactly:

- status `incomplete`, `covered:false`, no delivered body;
- all eight family predicates recorded (each `boundary_kind` clause `unknown`);
- the reason given is "do not invent or coerce caller facts";
- integer `3` is treated as unknown, not coerced.

Neither default (ordinary work, or acceptance) occurs. I revise my expectation to match the source.

Two related notes:
- The Writer's unknown-boundary unit test calls `compile_context` directly. It shows W35 as `unknown` with a gap on the core path; that test does not exercise the installed catalog route. Both paths fail closed.
- **G1 (by code reading only):** a misspelled value such as `"acceptance"` gives family `false` through the catalog route, which returns `refused`. It does not silently drop W35. A direct core caller bypassing the catalog would drop W35 (A1, adjacent). Neither was observed.

# RC2 declared prepublication claim closure

The [owner instruction and Writer grants](ACTIVATION.md) authorize this bounded
corrective release. Native A is `21a9d4b93c5adef1e84a369360a99176b98793c5`,
manifest `b691b0249c82ff39033ae636c4eaa0ab44bafee3732c79a227eb9409d53776c4`.
The source carrier B will be the commit containing this record. Neither this
record nor a version selector constitutes human exact-cut acceptance.

W35 now selects successor conservation at `product_acceptance`, preserving
qualification/release selection, ordinary-work exclusion and dependency guards.
The [153-rule predecessor ledger](PREDECESSOR_DISPOSITIONS.json) records 152
unchanged rules and the superseded W35 guard; rule text and dependencies remain
unchanged. The [actual independent Claude assessment](assessment/semantic-01/ASSESSMENT.md)
finds no material counterexample and supports six exact query subjects. The
[six runtime envelopes](assessment/semantic-01/assessments/) serialize those
actual judgments; they are not Writer-authored support. The packaged index keeps
its unassessed standing until a matching external assessment is supplied.

The following completed checks support the declared prepublication claims:

| Evidence | Observed result and scope |
|---|---|
| [Native comparison](method/SOURCE_DELTA.json) | 90 of 94 members equal RC1; four navigation/release metadata changes. Constitutional owners, defaults, frames and native workflow contracts unchanged. |
| [Frame test log](method/frame-tests.stderr) and [package check](method/PACKAGE_CHECK.json) | 52 tests pass; all 13 frames reproduce. |
| [Guide findings](method/GUIDE_FINDINGS.json) | Both former 35-rule statements and the missing helper were already repaired in RC1; current repairs preserved and checked. |
| [Context return](context/RESULT.json) and [freeze](context/FINAL_FREEZE.json) | 28 preserved controls and eight new boundary controls pass; 136 source members and 86 portable members frozen. |
| [Assessed archive replay](assessed-packaged/RESULT.json) | 80/80 operations pass. All six exact queries are covered on Codex and Claude layouts; missing, null and integer boundary facts refuse without delivery. Receipt-owned removal passes. |
| [Archive extraction](PRODUCT_EXTRACTION.json) | All 225 companion members match the assembled archive inventory and actual native pin. |
| [Manager check](manager-checks/RESULT.json) | New 3.1.0rc2 wheel matches owned source; version metadata is the only manager change. Third-party wheel bytes conserved; offline hash-locked installation and verification pass. |
| [Visual return](visual/RESULT.json) and [comparison](visual/PREDECESSOR_COMPARISON.json) | Selected source meanings and 306 records conserved under explicit identity mapping; six pipeline operations, nine public controls and 12 offline browser checks pass. |
| [Git transaction tests](ref-tests-01/RESULT.json) | Eight checks pass, including stale lease, higher ordinal and incomplete graph refusal, server rejection without partial publication, and atomic 25-ref success preserving RC1. |

The independent semantic assessment retains R1-R4 and R6 compression/source
re-entry limits, A1 direct-core bypass and A2 integration-time disposition
limits, and the identified RC1 residuals. These are bounded/adjacent findings;
the assessor requires no further candidate repair for this release. Caller facts
remain observations to establish, including the fixture's Python version. The
actual Claude invocation retains its compaction event and supplied-context limits;
no adequate-attention or whole-host capacity claim follows from completion.
The visual artifact retains 94 empty structured re-entry arrays and textual
source re-entry. General fidelity, Graphify, automatic host pickup, code
correctness, universal coverage and whole-method qualification are not claimed.

The remaining publication conditions are explicit: freeze B; independently
assess the exact annotated local ref graph, package and source identities; bind
the final cohort asset and all six expected asset hashes; atomically publish the
25 leased refs with RC1 unchanged; publish the normal GitHub release; reacquire
all assets publicly; freshly install and replay the exact manager, native cut,
host adapters and visual artifact. C1 in the semantic assessment requires the
native release note's prospective assertions to match these actual outcomes.
Those effects are unperformed at this record's creation and must be recorded in
RELEASED.md and RESULT.json. Human exact-cut acceptance and consumer adoption
remain separate.

# STDO 3.1.0-rc.2

This corrective native cut belongs to public version line **STDO 3.1.0**.
Its immutable tag is `specification_methodology/v3.1.0-rc.2`, logical cut is
`stdo://releases/v3.1.0-rc.2/`, and moving selector is
`specification_methodology/v3.1.0`. Its exact native predecessor is
`specification_methodology/v3.1.0-rc.1`, commit
`c1e0faaa8437c169031a476343c764614135cd93`. RC1 remains immutable.

## Corrected capability and conservation

Purpose Context's SDLC index selects W35 at `product_acceptance`, as well as
`qualification` and `release`. A successor acceptance context carries the
existing duty to identify the exact immutable predecessor and disposition
each predecessor claim capable of affecting the successor. An unresolved
disposition blocks the affected acceptance claim. EVALUATION section 5 and
RELEASE section 9 already own this law; their bytes and meaning are unchanged.
A query or delivered context creates no acceptance authority.

All constitutional owners, default flow, generated frames and native workflow
skill contracts are conserved from RC1. Native changes are this release note
and acquisition/navigation version bindings. The manager has new version
metadata with unchanged behavior and third-party dependency bytes. RC1's
corrected guides and runnable frame suite remain in the source carrier.

## Release subject

The cohort retains six independent Products: Specification Methodology,
Purpose Context, STDO Skills, Representation Tools, STDO Representation and
Axiom Indexer. Owned versions use `3.1.0-rc.2`; the manager uses equivalent
PEP 440 version `3.1.0rc2`. The
[cohort record](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/download/specification_methodology%2Fv3.1.0-rc.2/cohort-release-v3.1.0-rc.2.json)
binds exact Product subjects, dependencies, assets, predecessor dispositions
and evidence. Native A precedes derived bindings and carrier B; the complete
ref set publishes in one guarded atomic transaction.

The native installation retains its standards, templates, default guidance,
frames, workflow plugin and [reading page](../standards/documentation/index.html).
The separate [Product archive](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/download/specification_methodology%2Fv3.1.0-rc.2/stdo-products-v3.1.0-rc.2.zip)
contains Purpose Context, Skills and optional visual Products. Both context
purposes and the retained visual interpretation bind actual native RC2 sources.
Earlier exact assets and assessments retain their original identities.
Follow [Getting Started](../plugins/spec/references/GETTING_STARTED.md#new-project)
for native acquisition and independent host installation.

## Evidence and adoption boundaries

The cohort record distinguishes failing RC1 acceptance, repaired boundary
selection, independent exact-query assessment, installed adapter checks,
package identity and public acquisition. Valid predecessor evidence is reused
only through explicit applicability. No universal query coverage, whole-method
qualification, automatic host pickup, whole-host context-fit or future task
correctness is established. Exact-cut human acceptance remains separate.

Existing consumers retain their installed basis, defaults and receipts until
their own authorized adoption. Publication changes no global installation.
Historical formal/Lean and combined context routes remain retired from this
cohort. The [licence](../LICENSE) and third-party notices apply.
